answer: A bond of 26% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in terrace, and island reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, an attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across 38 aliases, and each one needs its own funded raven account. That bill is paid per identity, so 284 aliases cost 88 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
